sanigamaṃ.meaning_2: together with the market towns; including the towns
sanigamaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text, agreeing with saraṭṭhakaṃ. sa- here is the prefix saha (with). PEU gives it as an adjective.
sanigamaṃ.translation_1: Having bowed to the citizens of country and town,
sanigamaṃ.translation_2: Having bowed to the king, to the people, and to the citizens of country and town;

kapirājacariyā.meaning_2: conduct of the monkey king; the monkey king's way of behaving
kapirājacariyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the seventh chapter of the Cariyāpiṭaka; nominative singular. Sometimes treated as a dvanda-style title rather than a straightforward compound.
kapirājacariyā.translation_1: 7. The Conduct of the Monkey King

saṅkhacariyā.meaning_2: the practice of the Brahmin Saṅkha; Saṅkha's conduct
saṅkhacariyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the second chapter of the Cariyāpiṭaka. Saṅkha is the name of the Brahmin who is a former life of the Buddha. Nominative singular.

jātettha.meaning_2: born here; born in this place
jātettha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] jāta (pp of jāyati) + ettha (here). The text reads jātettha vessavīthiyā: 'I was born here in the merchants' street.'
jātettha.translation_1: I was born there in the peasant’s street,
jātettha.translation_2: I was born there in the merchant’s street, and that’s why I was called Vessantara.

kapimāgantvā.meaning_2: a monkey, having come; having arrived, the monkey
kapimāgantvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of kapiṃ (accusative singular of kapi) and āgantvā (absolutive of āgacchati). Alternative analysis: kapi + māgantvā, but the sense in the Cariyāpiṭaka verse is 'a monkey having come'.
kapimāgantvā.translation_2: Then a monkey came along, wicked, ignoble, and nimble.

jinasevitaṃ.meaning_2: practised by the Victor; fostered by the Buddha; resorted to by the conqueror
jinasevitaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of jina (the Buddha) + sevita (practised, resorted to). In the text it agrees with pubbakaṃ dhammaṃ (masc accusative singular) and describes the ancient Dhamma as practised by former Buddhas.
jinasevitaṃ.translation_2: Recollecting the Dhamma of the good, the ancient way fostered by former Victors,

mātaṅgacariyaṃ.meaning_2: elephant conduct; the practice of the elephant; the elephant's way of life
mātaṅgacariyaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the seventh cariyā in the Cariyāpiṭaka, referring to the Buddha's former life as an elephant. Accusative singular in the text. Sometimes resolved as mātaṅga + cariyā (fem), 'the elephant's conduct'.

sapabbataṃ.meaning_2: with mountains; together with the mountains
sapabbataṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] sa- is the prefix form of saha ("with"). Accusative singular agreeing with pathaviṃ in the text.
sapabbataṃ.translation_2: The earth from sea to sea, with its forests and mountains—

paññāsasamādhikāni.meaning_2: more than fifty; fifty or more
paññāsasamādhikāni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it qualifies vassāni (neuter plural), so it appears as paññāsasamādhikāni. Sandhi paññāsā + samādhika > paññāsasamādhika.
paññāsasamādhikāni.example_2: Athāparaṃ yaṃ caritaṃ mamedaṃ, vassāni paññāsasamādhikāni.
paññāsasamādhikāni.translation_2: but then, as for this behavior (caritaṃ) of mine for more than fifty years,
